name: Hearts
intro: Learn Hearts from scratch: points, passing, following suit, the first trick, breaking hearts and shooting the moon, then ducking, dumping the queen, voids and stopping a moon.

units.name: How Hearts works
units.blurb: Passing, following suit, points, breaking hearts and shooting the moon.

lessons.title: Hearts: the aim and the points
lessons.summary: In Hearts you try to avoid points: every heart is 1 and the queen of spades is 13. Learn how tricks and points work.
lessons.wrap: Fewest points wins. Next: passing cards.

steps.text:
Hearts is played by four players, each for themselves, with 13 cards each. In each trick, the highest card of the suit led wins. There are no trumps.

The aim is to take as few points as possible: every heart is 1 point, and the queen of spades is 13. When someone reaches 100, the lowest score wins.
Quick check.
steps.prompt: How many points are there in each round?
steps.explain: 26: thirteen hearts at 1 point each, plus 13 for the queen of spades.

steps.text: Diamonds were led and there are no points in this trick, so winning it is harmless.
steps.wrong: Play a diamond higher than the jack.
steps.done: You win a trick with no points in it: no harm done.

lessons.title: Passing three cards
lessons.summary: Each round starts by passing three cards: left, right, across, then no pass. Learn which cards are dangerous and worth passing.
lessons.wrap: Pass the cards that could catch the queen or win heart tricks. Next: following suit and the first trick.

steps.text:
Before each round, everyone passes three cards to another player: to the left, then the right, then across, and every fourth round there’s no pass.

Pass the cards most likely to win you points: the queen of spades and the high spades (ace and king) that can be forced to take her, and high hearts.
Your spades are ace, king, queen and a 4. With so few low spades, the queen is likely to land on you.
steps.prompt: Tap the three most dangerous cards to pass.
steps.wrong: Look at your spades: the queen and the two cards that can be forced to win her.
steps.done: Queen, king and ace of spades: gone.

lessons.title: Following suit and the first trick
lessons.summary: In Hearts you must follow suit if you can, the two of clubs leads the first trick, and no points can be played on it. Learn the rules.
lessons.wrap: Follow suit; no points on the first trick. Next: breaking hearts.

steps.text: As in most card games, you must follow suit if you can.
steps.prompt: Clubs were led. Tap every card you may play.
steps.wrong: You have clubs, so you must play one.

steps.text:
The player with the two of clubs leads the first trick. On that first trick nobody may play a heart or the queen of spades unless they have nothing else.

You have no clubs.
steps.prompt: Tap every card you may play on the first trick.
steps.wrong: No points on the first trick while you have something else.

lessons.title: Breaking hearts
lessons.summary: You can’t lead a heart until hearts are broken, when someone has played one on another suit. Learn which cards you can lead.
lessons.wrap: Hearts open up once one has been played. Next: shooting the moon.

steps.text: You’re leading, and nobody has played a heart yet. Hearts aren’t broken, so you can’t lead one (unless you have nothing but hearts).
steps.prompt: Tap every card you may lead.

steps.text: Now someone has discarded a heart on another suit.
steps.prompt: Tap every card you may lead.
steps.wrong: Once hearts are broken, you can lead anything.

lessons.title: Shooting the moon
lessons.summary: Take every heart and the queen of spades in one round and you score nothing, while everyone else gets 26. Learn how shooting the moon works.
lessons.wrap: You know every rule. Test yourself in the rules check.

position.hand: AH KH QH JH 10H AS KS AD KD QD AC KC QC

steps.text:
If one player takes all 13 hearts and the queen of spades in a round, they’ve shot the moon: they score 0, and every other player gets 26 points.

It’s a big gamble. If you take nearly all the points but someone else takes one heart, you’re left with a huge score.
You shoot the moon.
steps.prompt: What do the other three players score this round?

units.blurb: Five questions on the rules. Pass to unlock the strategy.

lessons.title: Hearts rules check
lessons.summary: Test your Hearts rules: points, passing, following suit, the first trick, breaking hearts and shooting the moon.
lessons.wrap: Rules check passed. Now for staying out of trouble.

steps.text: Question 1.
steps.prompt: How many points is the queen of spades worth?

steps.text: Question 2.
steps.prompt: Diamonds were led. Tap every card you may play.

steps.text: Question 3. Hearts aren’t broken.
steps.prompt: Tap every card you may lead.
steps.wrong: You can’t lead a heart yet.

steps.text: Question 5.

units.name: Staying out of trouble
units.blurb: Ducking, dumping the queen, voids and stopping a moon.

lessons.title: Duck under the winning card
lessons.summary: When a trick could have points in it, play a card just below the one that’s winning. Learn to duck and keep the dangerous tricks away from you.
lessons.wrap: Play your highest card that still loses the trick.

steps.text:
Someone has already dropped a heart on this trick, so whoever wins it takes a point. The king of diamonds is winning.

Play a diamond under the king, and the trick goes to someone else. Using your highest card that still loses (here the 9) gets rid of a dangerous middle card too.
Keep the heart away from you.
steps.prompt: Play a card that doesn’t win the trick.
steps.wrong: Your ace would win, and take the heart with it. Play under the king.
steps.done: Ducked. Someone else takes the heart.

lessons.title: Dump the queen of spades
lessons.summary: When you can’t follow suit, it’s your chance to get rid of the queen of spades on someone else’s trick. Learn to spot it.
lessons.wrap: No cards in the suit led? Give away your worst card: the queen first.

steps.text: You have no diamonds, so you can play anything, and the trick will go to someone else. That’s the moment to dump your most dangerous card on them.
The ace of diamonds is winning.
steps.wrong: The queen of spades is worth 13 points. Give it away now.
steps.done: The queen goes to the player who led the ace: 13 points for them.

lessons.title: Make a void
lessons.summary: A suit you have none of lets you throw away dangerous cards whenever it’s led. Learn why emptying a short suit early helps in Hearts.
lessons.wrap: Get rid of short suits early, and use the voids to dump your dangerous cards.

steps.text:
Having no cards in a suit, a void, is powerful in Hearts: whenever that suit is led, you can throw away the queen of spades or a high heart.

Short suits are the easiest to empty, so passing or playing them early can set up a void.
You’re passing three cards.
steps.prompt: Which pass could give you a void?
steps.explain: All three diamonds: with none left, you can dump the queen whenever diamonds are led.

lessons.title: Stopping a moon
lessons.summary: If one player is taking every point, take a single heart yourself to stop them shooting the moon. Learn when it’s worth it.
lessons.wrap: One point for you can save 26 for everyone.

steps.text: One player has taken every heart so far and the queen of spades. It looks like they’re shooting the moon.
options: Win a trick with a heart in it, to take at least one point
steps.explain: Take one point. You score 1 or 2, and they can’t give everyone 26.
